name: E-3 Sentry (AWACS)
summary: Four-engine airborne warning and control aircraft built on the Boeing 707-320 airframe, carrying a large rotating radar dome; a dwindling fleet awaiting the E-7.

engines: Four long, slender low-bypass engines in narrow nacelles on pylons
Engines noticeably thinner than those on re-engined KC-135s
fuselage: Narrowbody airliner-shaped fuselage with very few windows
Large flat radar disc (rotodome) mounted on two struts above the rear fuselage
Refueling receptacle on top behind the cockpit
tail: Tall swept single fin with a probe at the tip

tellTales: Large disc radar on struts above the rear fuselage of a four-engine jet
Narrowbody airliner shape with almost no windows

confusedWith.howToTell: The E-3 is a large four-jet airliner shape; the E-2 is a small twin-turboprop carrier aircraft with a four-fin tail.
The E-3 carries a large radar disc on struts and has slimmer engines; the KC-135 has no disc and a refueling boom.
The E-3 has a radar disc above the fuselage; the E-6 has no disc but has pods at its wingtips.

usCount.source: FY2026 NDAA retirement freeze (16 aircraft) less one lost in March 2026, per The War Zone
